Hi Julia — appreciate the clear asks. High level: yes, we can support a split retention model and provide deletion certification; below is a pragmatic proposal to put into the order form so your legal team can review.

Retention model (proposal):
- Application outputs & model-generated artifacts: configurable rolling retention with a default of 90 days. Customer may set retention to a shorter window via console or API.
- Audit logs & billing records: retained in immutable, exportable form for up to 24 months (read-only access & export on request).

Deletion & certification (proposal):
- Primary deletion: upon customer request or contract expiry, Redwood will remove customer data from active production systems within 7 business days and provide an initial deletion acknowledgement.
- Backup/archives: backups will be scheduled for secure purge; Redwood guarantees deletion from backups within 30 calendar days from the deletion request for standard backups. For long-term archival snapshots (if any), Redwood will schedule secure purge within 90 days unless otherwise agreed.
- Certification: Redwood will provide a signed Deletion Certificate (PDF) that lists the data types deleted, systems purged, and the timestamp. Standard timeline: certificate issued within 5 business days after completion of deletion activities.

Notes & ask:
- Does MediCorps require that the 30-day backup purge timeline be shortened to 30 calendar days for all archival variants? If so, we need to confirm whether any existing retention holds (legal/govt) apply.
- We attached a short proposal (rdw-medicorps-data-retention-proposal.pdf) with suggested SLA language that Neha will formalize.

If that sounds roughly right, Neha (cc'd) will prepare an order form amendment you can share with legal. Ben will coordinate any billing/price implications for extended audit retention.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if you prefer to walk through specifics.

Hi Julia — looping in formal legal language below. I've drafted a concise Order Form amendment that you can include as an appendix. Key points cover the split retention, deletion timelines, and certificate language requested.

Proposed Order Form amendment (excerpt):
"Customer Data Retention and Deletion. Redwood will retain Customer Data as set out in the Service Configuration. Notwithstanding the foregoing:
(a) Model outputs and derived artifacts (\"Transitory Data\") will be retained for a configurable rolling window with a default of 90 days.
(b) Audit logs and billing records (\"Audit Data\") will be retained for twenty-four (24) months in a machine-readable, exportable format.
(c) Upon Customer's written request or termination, Redwood will initiate deletion of Customer Data from active systems within seven (7) business days and from standard backups within thirty (30) calendar days. For archival snapshots that require manual purge, Redwood will complete secure deletion within ninety (90) calendar days unless otherwise specified in writing.

Deletion Certification. Upon completion of deletion activities, Redwood will issue a signed Deletion Certificate within five (5) business days. The Certificate will include: (i) description of data categories deleted; (ii) affected system identifiers and deletion job IDs; (iii) applicable object keys or IDs where feasible; and (iv) a statement confirming the deletion process and the effective deletion timestamp.

Exceptions & Holds: Deletion timelines are subject to court order, statutory hold, or explicit, written retention hold imposed by Customer; Redwood will notify Customer if any such hold prevents immediate deletion.
"

On the technical points:
- We can include unique object IDs and deletion job IDs in the certificate; for irrecoverability hashes, we can include a best-effort SHA256 digest of the deletion manifest where applicable, but we cannot provide irreversible proofs for hardware-level overwrites for certain third-party archival vendors. We call that out in the exception language above.
- KV caches and derived embeddings: by default we treat derived artifacts as Customer Data for deletion requests and will purge them in the same workflow.

Next steps I propose:
1) Julia — please confirm MediCorps accepts the 30-day standard backup purge as the maximum and if any internal holds apply.
2) Monica/Ben — Ben, flag any pricing impact for keeping 24-month audit retention; I'll draft final amendment once pricing/term guidance is confirmed.

Happy to jump on a quick call if the certificate format needs tweaking (we can provide a template PDF).

Regards,
